goal: A worktree created outside scripts/susi-worktree.sh inherits the creating tree's susi.agent, so two worktrees answer to one identity and can renew, close and release each other's claims. It is live here: the primary checkout and a hand-made worktree under .claude/worktrees both carry PRIMARY, and a claim taken in one was attributable to both. The readiness board reports it but does not block it, and a report is not a guard. Refuse a commit from a worktree whose token another worktree also carries, name the offenders, and print the ordered fix - the claim has to be released and re-claimed because a claim travels with its token. DONE, and the obstacle recorded in the first attempt is what diagnosed it: the script is written, proven three ways (a plain run; a run with GIT_DIR exported exactly as a hook sees it; a run from the PRIMARY-sharing worktree, which refuses and names the primary), wired into commit-msg, and the suite that had blocked the wiring passes 6/6. That failure was the fixture, not the guard: tests/hook_enforcement.rs copies a fixed list of hook dependencies into its temp repo, so the hook's new call had no script to run - the list now includes it.
title: One token per worker, enforced at commit time
